metadata.notes: CUT is one verb with a 'shape' parameter (CLAUDE_DEV_CTX.md's 4th pillar, Parameters), not five separate verbs — the resulting state is whatever shape was chosen, so allowedValues doubles as the set of post-cut states.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — re-cutting already-cut pieces just re-asserts/changes the shape parameter, no duplication risk (no byproducts spawned).
metadata.halvedQuarteredNote: Added 2026-08-14, directly in response to boiling potato: 'halved'/'quartered' are the real, common whole-but-reduced boiling/roasting prep sizes (see potato-doneness.ts's POTATO_BOIL_DONENESS, whose 'halved_or_quartered' pieceSize category needed a real corresponding CUT state to attach to — potato.json previously had no way to represent this size at all, only 'sliced'/'diced'/'julienne'/'chopped'/'minced', none of which are what a real recipe means by 'quartered potatoes for boiling'). No per-entity restriction on this shared enum (see egg.json's cutNote for the same, already-named limitation) — nothing stops requesting a 'julienne' or 'halved' egg either, an existing, real, unscoped gap this addition doesn't close, just doesn't make worse.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): LOOKS similar to mash.json/grate.json (repeated mechanical tool strokes) but is genuinely different: CUT produces a FIXED, predetermined geometric target (a specific shape/size) via a bounded number of strokes, not an open-ended do-until threshold crossed by 'more of the same' — you don't 'keep cutting until diced' the way you 'keep mashing until smooth'. verification.confidence is 'high' precisely because completion is reliably, discretely checkable, unlike the paper's stated instantaneous rationale ('completion cannot be reliably sensed') — a genuine, worth-naming tension with the paper's own justification for the class, even though the classification itself (instantaneous) is correct on the deeper 'bounded discrete act vs. accumulating process' test. Both discriminators actually AGREE here once examined carefully (not a real disagreement, despite initially looking ambiguous) — action.ts's own doc comment uses this exact action as the reason duration:'variable' is not the same axis as actionKind.

hazards.note: Repeated blade motion directly against the target — the closest sustained hand-to-blade proximity of any action in this vocabulary
